samples.summary: copyThread detaches anchors with detachYorkieValue, which yorkie-json.ts documents as wrong for shapes containing nested arrays — docs (`posRange`) and pdf-text (`rects`) anchors are exactly that, so the flat-root paths this delta newly covers return CRDT metadata instead of the anchor
samples.evidence: `copyThread` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts:99) runs `detachYorkieValue(t.anchor)`. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:16-20` states the opposite contract in the repo's own words: "it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata". Docs anchors carry `posRange` as a Yorkie array (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:83-88 explicitly keeps it as a live proxy), and PDF text anchors carry `rects` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:56-64). Against a live CRDT the `GET /comments` list and every returned thread for a `doc` (and for a `pdf-text` thread) would therefore hand the CLI (`CommentThread.anchor`, packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:167-178) `{createdAt, movedAt}` in place of the anchor. The new `describe.each` fixtures seed plain objects (`{ kind: 'docs-range', blockId: 'b1' }`, no `posRange`; a plain `rect`), so the doc/pdf coverage this delta adds cannot surface it.

samples.summary: The agent-facing CLI schema still describes comment delete/edit as unconditionally available; it was not updated for the author-only 403 the API now enforces, and there is no `comments.edit` entry for the new PATCH comment route
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:487-508 documents `comments.delete` and `comments.delete-comment` with no mention that the server now refuses a comment the caller did not author (`assertCommentAuthor`, packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.ts:519-534, throwing ForbiddenException). The registry is the surface agents plan against, so a plan that deletes a peer's thread is described as valid and fails at runtime. Additionally `PATCH :threadId/comments/:commentId` (comments.controller.ts:406) has no CLI command in packages/cli/src/commands/comments.ts and no registry entry, so the route is unreachable from the CLI while every sibling comment route is exposed.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. comment-ops.ts:99 does call detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) inside copyThread. yorkie-json.ts:13-20 documents, and yorkie-json.ts:172-185 implements, the exact defect claimed: the helper branches on Array.isArray, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so such values fall into the Object.entries branch and come back as CRDT internals. Docs anchors do carry posRange as a live Yorkie array (yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-87, 97; types/comments.ts:31) and pdf-text anchors carry rects (pdf-comment-store.ts:56-64, whose field-by-field copyAnchor exists to avoid exactly this). The path is reachable against a real CRDT: comments.controller.ts:250-257 calls listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) for doc/pdf, and yorkie.service.ts:36-57 attaches a live yorkie.Document and passes the live proxy to the callback; listThreads calls copyThread at comment-ops.ts:139. No guard converts or unwraps the anchor beforehand. So GET /comments and every thread response for a doc (and a pdf-text thread) hands consumers CRDT metadata in place of posRange/rects. Same file already avoids Array.isArray for comments (comment-ops.ts:100,125-130), showing the hazard is known; the anchor is the un-fixed site. Real, reachable, wrong data returned to other consumers — major, not refutable.
